CHEM 101.description: A science elective surveying inorganic and solution chemistry. First of a terminal two-semester sequence. Three lecture, one recitation, and two laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 101.subject: CHEM
CHEM 101.title: Fundamental Chemistry I

CHEM 102.description: An introductory survey of organic and biochemistry. Three lecture, one recitation, and two laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 102.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 1 year high-school chemistry, CHEM 101, CHEM 111, or equivalent.
CHEM 102.subject: CHEM
CHEM 102.title: Fundamental Chemistry II

CHEM 105.description: A conceptual and qualitative approach to chemistry, its evolution, achievements, and goals and its impact on technology, the environment, and modern life and thought. (Specifically designed for non-science majors.) Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 105.subject: CHEM
CHEM 105.title: Chemistry and Modern Society I

CHEM 106.description: Introduction to general, organic, and analytical chemistry principles; chemical characteristics of organic compounds related to synthetic and natural drugs; application of analytical techniques for drug identification; includes readings, lectures, laboratory experiments, and demonstrations.
CHEM 106.subject: CHEM
CHEM 106.title: Chemistry and Modern Society II

CHEM 107.description: Surveys chemical aspects of criminal investigation and adjudication including drug, arson, DNA, paint, and fiber identification.
CHEM 107.subject: CHEM
CHEM 107.title: Introduction to Forensic Science

CHEM 107L.description: An analytical approach to surveys of criminal investigation and adjudication of crime scene analysis and collection and preservation of evidence. Analysis will include but not be limited to drug, arson, DNA, fingerprints, blood splatter, and fiber identification. Note: Three laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 107L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 107L.title: Introduction to Forensic Science Laboratory

CHEM 111.description: Survey of the principles that underlie all chemistry with applications illustrating these principles. Three lecture and one recitation hours per week.
CHEM 111.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 111 or higher (or by placement score into MATH 115 or higher).
CHEM 111.subject: CHEM
CHEM 111.title: General Chemistry I

CHEM 111L.description: Introduction to the principles and techniques of experimental chemistry with emphasis on formula investigations, equations, elementary statistics, and chemical reactivity.
CHEM 111L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 111L.title: General Chemistry I Lab

CHEM 112.description: Continuation of CHEM 111 . Special emphasis on chemical equilibrium. Three lecture and one recitation hours per week.
CHEM 112.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 111 or higher MATH (or by placement score into MATH 115 or higher).
CHEM 112.subject: CHEM
CHEM 112.title: General Chemistry II

CHEM 112L.description: Continuation of CHEM 111L with emphasis on solution properties, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, and qualitative analysis.
CHEM 112L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 111L or CHEM 141L.
CHEM 112L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 112L.title: General Chemistry II Lab

CHEM 118.description: Introduction to the use of computers in solving chemical problems. One discussion and two laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 118.subject: CHEM
CHEM 118.title: Computational Chemistry I

CHEM 141.description: Advanced general chemistry I. Atoms and chemical bonds. Three lecture hours, one recitation hour per week. Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 111 and CHEM 141.
CHEM 141.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 111 or placement into MATH 115 or higher MATH.
CHEM 141.subject: CHEM
CHEM 141.title: Principles of Chemistry I

CHEM 141L.description: This laboratory-based course supports and extends key topics in principles of general chemistry, with a focus on the experimental investigation of atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, chemical reactions, thermodynamics, gas laws, and intermolecular forces.
CHEM 141L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 111 or placement into MATH 115 or higher MATH.
CHEM 141L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 141L.title: Principles of Chemistry I Laboratory

CHEM 142.description: Advanced general chemistry II. Chemical kinetics, equilibria, and thermodynamics. Three lecture hours, one recitation hour per week. Note: Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 112 and CHEM 142.
CHEM 142.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 115 (or by placement score into MATH 141 or higher); C or higher in CHEM 141 or CHEM 112.
CHEM 142.subject: CHEM
CHEM 142.title: Principles of Chemistry II

CHEM 142L.description: Advanced general chemistry II laboratory. Chemical kinetics, equilibria, and thermodynamics. Three laboratory hours per week. Note: Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 112L and CHEM 142L.
CHEM 142L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 115 (or by placement score into MATH 141 or higher); C or higher in CHEM 141 or CHEM 112.
CHEM 142L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 142L.title: Principles of Chemistry II Laboratory

CHEM 198.description: Fundamental laboratory and professional research training emphasizing lab safety, solution preparation, data collection, and operation of UV-Vis, fluorescence, and FT-IR spectroscopic instrumentation. Includes development of scientific communication skills, understanding of research ethics, literature analysis, and career preparation.
CHEM 198.subject: CHEM
CHEM 198.title: Undergraduate Research Initiative: Foundations of Scientific Research

CHEM 199.description: Advanced laboratory methods in cyclic voltammetry, nanoparticle synthesis, and computational chemistry. Emphasis on research communication, graduate school preparation, and professional engagement through faculty presentations and the Discover USC event.
CHEM 199.subject: CHEM
CHEM 199.title: Undergraduate Research Initiative: From Data to Discovery

CHEM 318.description: A continuation of CHEM 118 , with applications to more advanced chemical problems. One discussion and two laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 318.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CSCE 145 or CSCE 106 and in CHEM 118.
CHEM 318.subject: CHEM
CHEM 318.title: Computational Chemistry II

CHEM 321.description: Gravimetric, volumetric, and introductory instrumental analysis. Three lecture and one recitation hours per week.
CHEM 321.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 or CHEM 142; C or higher in MATH 111 (or by placement score in MATH 115 or higher).
CHEM 321.subject: CHEM
CHEM 321.title: Quantitative Analysis

CHEM 321L.description: Laboratory methods supporting Gravimetric, volumetric, and introductory instrumental analysis. Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 321L and CHEM 322L .
CHEM 321L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112L or CHEM 142L.
CHEM 321L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 321L.title: Quantitative Analysis Laboratory

CHEM 322.description: Qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis, fundamental or method analysis, and molecular characterization.
CHEM 322.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 or CHEM 142; C or higher in MATH 111 or higher (or placement in MATH 115 or higher).
CHEM 322.subject: CHEM
CHEM 322.title: Analytical Chemistry

CHEM 322L.description: Laboratory skill building in analytical techniques. Applications of stoichiometry, spectroscopy, phase transfer, electrochemistry and kinetics. Credit cannot be received for both CHEM 321L and CHEM 322L.
CHEM 322L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112L or CHEM 142L.
CHEM 322L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 322L.title: Analytical Chemistry Laboratory

CHEM 331L.description: Laboratory safety, syntheses, separation, and purification of carbon compounds. For non-majors.
CHEM 331L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 112L or CHEM 142L.
CHEM 331L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 331L.title: Essentials of Organic Chemistry Laboratory I

CHEM 332L.description: Continuation of CHEM 331L . Spectroscopic identification of carbon compounds. For non-majors. Three lab hours per week.
CHEM 332L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 331L.
CHEM 332L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 332L.title: Essentials of Organic Chemistry Laboratory II

CHEM 333.description: Contemporary theories, nomenclature, reactions, mechanisms, and syntheses of carbon compounds. Three lecture and one recitation hours per week.
CHEM 333.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 or in CHEM 142.
CHEM 333.subject: CHEM
CHEM 333.title: Organic Chemistry I

CHEM 333L.description: Laboratory safety, synthesis, separation, and purification of carbon compounds. Required for chemistry majors. Six laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 333L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 112L or CHEM 142L.
CHEM 333L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 333L.title: Comprehensive Organic Chemistry Laboratory I

CHEM 334.description: Continuation of CHEM 333 . Three lecture and one recitation hours per week.
CHEM 334.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 333.
CHEM 334.subject: CHEM
CHEM 334.title: Organic Chemistry II

CHEM 334L.description: Continuation of CHEM 333L . Spectroscopic identification of carbon compounds. Required for chemistry majors. Six laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 334L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 333L.
CHEM 334L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 334L.title: Comprehensive Organic Chemistry Laboratory II

CHEM 340.description: A non-calculus approach to the study of the principles of physical chemistry emphasizing their application to significant biochemical and biological systems. Chemical thermodynamics, kinetics, equilibrium, solution chemistry, the structure of macromolecules, and acid-base properties of biomolecules. Credit for a degree will not be given for both CHEM 340 and CHEM 541 .
CHEM 340.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 and CHEM 112L or in CHEM 142.
CHEM 340.subject: CHEM
CHEM 340.title: Elementary Biophysical Chemistry

CHEM 360.description: Student seminars and a survey of biochemical and molecular biology research at the University of South Carolina. Required of all biochemistry majors.
CHEM 360.subject: CHEM
CHEM 360.title: Undergraduate Seminar

CHEM 401.description: Prepares students for future roles in chemical industry or graduate school and provides career-enhancing interpersonal skills, including team-building, public speaking, resume preparation, and interviewing.
CHEM 401.subject: CHEM
CHEM 401.title: Industrial Chemistry Capstone Experience

CHEM 496.description: Introduction to the methods of chemical research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester. Nine hours of library and laboratory per week. Contract Required.
CHEM 496.subject: CHEM
CHEM 496.title: Undergraduate Research

CHEM 497.description: Introduction to the methods of chemical research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester. Nine hours of library and laboratory per week. Contract Required.
CHEM 497.subject: CHEM
CHEM 497.title: Undergraduate Research

CHEM 498.description: Introduction to the methods of chemical research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester. Nine hours of library and laboratory per week. Contract Required.
CHEM 498.subject: CHEM
CHEM 498.title: Undergraduate Research

CHEM 499.description: Introduction to the methods of chemical research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester. Nine hours of library and laboratory per week. Contract Required.
CHEM 499.subject: CHEM
CHEM 499.title: Undergraduate Research

CHEM 511.description: Consideration of atomic structure, valence, complex compounds, and systematic study of the periodic table.
CHEM 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334, PHYS 212, and MATH 241.
CHEM 511.subject: CHEM
CHEM 511.title: Inorganic Chemistry

CHEM 533.description: Selected organic reactions from synthetic and mechanistic viewpoints. For Undergraduate Credit Only.
CHEM 533.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334.
CHEM 533.subject: CHEM
CHEM 533.title: Comprehensive Organic Chemistry III

CHEM 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 or CHEM 142; C or higher in MATH 241 or department permission.
CHEM 541.subject: CHEM
CHEM 541.title: Physical Chemistry I: Thermodynamics and Kinetics

CHEM 541L.description: Applications of physical chemical techniques in Thermodynamics and Kinetics. Five laboratory hours and one recitation hour per week.
CHEM 541L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 321L or CHEM 322L, or departmental permission.
CHEM 541L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 541L.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory I: Thermodynamics and Kinetics

CHEM 542.description: Spectroscopy, statistical mechanics, and chemical applications of quantum mechanics.
CHEM 542.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 112 or CHEM 142; C or higher in MATH 241 and PHYS 212, or departmental approval.
CHEM 542.subject: CHEM
CHEM 542.title: Physical Chemistry II: Quantum Mechanics and Spectroscopy

CHEM 542L.description: Applications of physical chemical techniques in quantum mechanics and spectroscopy. Five laboratory hours and one recitation hour per week.
CHEM 542L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 321L or CHEM 322L or by departmental permission.
CHEM 542L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 542L.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory II: Quantum Mechanics and Spectroscopy

CHEM 545.description: A survey of physical methods essential for studies of biomacromolecules. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 545.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 541 and in CHEM 550 or CHEM 555.
CHEM 545.subject: CHEM
CHEM 545.title: Physical Biochemistry

CHEM 550.description: Description of biological macromolecules and major metabolic pathways.
CHEM 550.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334.
CHEM 550.subject: CHEM
CHEM 550.title: Biochemistry

CHEM 550L.description: Experiments and demonstrations illustrating the principles of biochemistry. Three laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 550L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 550L.title: Biochemistry Laboratory

CHEM 555.description: Comprehensive introduction to the structure and function of major biological macromolecules—amino acids, proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids. Topics include enzyme catalysis, kinetics, inhibition, and core metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the citric acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism. Concludes with an integrated study of mammalian fuel metabolism and the regulation and coordination of metabolic pathways.
CHEM 555.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334, or departmental permission.
CHEM 555.subject: CHEM
CHEM 555.title: Protein Biochemistry and Metabolism

CHEM 556.description: Examination of key topics in molecular biology, including DNA and RNA metabolism, regulation of gene expression at transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels, protein synthesis, and mechanisms of cell cycle control and cancer development. Includes principles and applications of recombinant DNA technology.
CHEM 556.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 302, or departmental approval.
CHEM 556.subject: CHEM
CHEM 556.title: Molecular Biochemistry of the Cell

CHEM 619.description: Current developments in inorganic chemistry. Readings and research on selected topics. Course content varies by title and will be announced in the schedule of classes. May be repeated for credit.
CHEM 619.subject: CHEM
CHEM 619.title: Special Topics in Inorganic Chemistry

CHEM 621.description: Chemical instrumentation including electronics, signal processing, statistical analysis, molecular/atomic spectroscopy, electrochemical methods, chromatography, and mass spectrometry. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 621.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 321 or CHEM 322.
CHEM 621.subject: CHEM
CHEM 621.title: Instrumental Analysis

CHEM 621L.description: Methods, principles and strategies for chemical instrumentation in analysis. Chemical instrumentation laboratory with environmental, forensic, and biotechnology applications. Three laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 621L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 621L.title: Instrumental Analysis Lab

CHEM 622.description: Analytical chemical methods in forensic science, including gathering of evidence, toxicology, drug identification, analysis of trace evidence, arson analysis, and DNA/serology. Three lecture hours and three laboratory hours per week.
CHEM 622.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 321 and CHEM 321L or CHEM 322 and CHEM 322L; C or higher in CHEM 334; C or higher in CHEM 332L or CHEM 334L.
CHEM 622.subject: CHEM
CHEM 622.title: Forensic Analytical Chemistry

CHEM 623.description: Study of the chemical reactions and processes that affect the fate and transport of organic chemicals in the environment. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 623.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 321, in CHEM 333, and in MATH 142.
CHEM 623.subject: CHEM
CHEM 623.title: Introductory Environmental Chemistry

CHEM 624.description: Study of the chemical reactions and processes affecting the distribution of chemical species in natural systems. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 624.subject: CHEM
CHEM 624.title: Aquatic Chemistry

CHEM 629.description: Current developments in inorganic chemistry. Readings and research on selected topics. Course content varies by title and will be announced in the schedule of classes. May be repeated for credit.
CHEM 629.subject: CHEM
CHEM 629.title: Special Topics in Analytical Chemistry

CHEM 633.description: Special emphasis on the modern synthesis of polymeric materials. Definitions, characterization, and applications of polymers will be briefly presented.
CHEM 633.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334.
CHEM 633.subject: CHEM
CHEM 633.title: Introduction to Polymer Synthesis

CHEM 639.description: Current developments in organic chemistry. Readings and research on selected topics. May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 639.subject: CHEM
CHEM 639.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry

CHEM 643.description: This course is designed to familiarize students with theory and use of modern electronic structure codes, as well as to develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills and to improve computer literacy.
CHEM 643.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 541 or CHEM 542.
CHEM 643.subject: CHEM
CHEM 643.title: Computational Chemistry

CHEM 644.description: Introduction to materials science; structural and electronic description of inorganic-based solids; experimental techniques in materials chemistry; interfacial energetics and optoelectronic processes at metal and semiconductor surfaces.
CHEM 644.subject: CHEM
CHEM 644.title: Materials Chemistry

CHEM 649.description: Current developments in physical chemistry. Readings and research on selected topics. Course content varies by title and will be announced in the schedule of classes. May be repeated for credit.
CHEM 649.subject: CHEM
CHEM 649.title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry

CHEM 655.description: Core concepts of biochemistry as applied to human health and disease.
CHEM 655.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 555/BIOL 545 or CHEM 550/BIOL 541.
CHEM 655.subject: CHEM
CHEM 655.title: Metabolic Biochemistry of Human Disease

CHEM 659.description: Selected topics in the field of biochemistry. May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 659.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 555/BIOL 545 or CHEM 550/BIOL 541.
CHEM 659.subject: CHEM
CHEM 659.title: Special Topics in Biochemistry

CHEM 700.description: Various approaches to solving problems in gas laws, solution chemistry, and equilibrium. Comparison of the pedagogical merits of the different approaches. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.Students. Three lectures per week.
CHEM 700.subject: CHEM
CHEM 700.title: Methods of Solving Problems in Chemistry

CHEM 701.description: Required of all graduate students. Fall or Spring limit of 2 credits.
CHEM 701.subject: CHEM
CHEM 701.title: Seminar

CHEM 701A.description: A survey of chemical research at the University of South Carolina. Required of all first-year degree candidates in chemistry.
CHEM 701A.subject: CHEM
CHEM 701A.title: Seminar

CHEM 702.description: Covalent bonding in compounds of the first short period elements, with emphasis on those of boron, carbon, and nitrogen. Structure of molecules, some important functional groups, resonance in unsaturated compounds, stereochemistry, and organometallic compounds. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., or M.Ed. students. Three lectures and one discussion period per week.
CHEM 702.subject: CHEM
CHEM 702.title: Structure and Bonding in Covalent Molecules

CHEM 703.description: General types of organic reactions, including those of biochemistry. Industrial preparations of both organic and inorganic compounds of major importance. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., or M.Ed. students. Three lectures and one discussion period per week.
CHEM 703.subject: CHEM
CHEM 703.title: Molecular Reactions

CHEM 704.description: The basic laws of chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, and equilibrium, with emphasis on the practical and theoretical importance of the interconversion of chemical energy with other forms of energy. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., or M.Ed. students. Three lectures and one discussion period per week.
CHEM 704.subject: CHEM
CHEM 704.title: Energy, Equilibrium, and Chemical Change

CHEM 705.description: A survey of the applications of modern instrumental techniques to the solution of chemical problems, with emphasis on development of a basic understanding of the experiment and on interpretation of data. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., or M.Ed. students. Three lectures and one discussion period per week.
CHEM 705.subject: CHEM
CHEM 705.title: Modern Instrumental Methods in Chemistry

CHEM 706.description: The structures and functions of proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, enzymes, and other biologically important molecules; the role of these molecules in the major metabolic pathways. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., or M.Ed. students. Three lectures and one discussion period per week.
CHEM 706.subject: CHEM
CHEM 706.title: Chemistry in Living Systems

CHEM 709.description: Selected chemical topics with emphasis on modern chemical concepts. For teachers of chemistry, M.A.T., I.M.A. and M.Ed. students. Lectures, discussion, laboratories, depending on credit offered.
CHEM 709.subject: CHEM
CHEM 709.title: Special Topics in Chemical Education

CHEM 711.description: The use and interpretation of modern physical measurements of particular application to inorganic chemistry, including X-ray, ESR, magnetic measurements, Mössbauer spectra, ligand field theory, and reaction mechanisms.
CHEM 711.subject: CHEM
CHEM 711.title: Physical-Inorganic Chemistry

CHEM 712.description: Systematic study of the reactions and bonding of the d and f transition elements.
CHEM 712.subject: CHEM
CHEM 712.title: The Chemistry of Transition Elements

CHEM 713.description: Systematic study of the structure and bonding of the inorganic compounds of main group elements.
CHEM 713.subject: CHEM
CHEM 713.title: The Chemistry of the Representative Elements

CHEM 719.description: May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 719.subject: CHEM
CHEM 719.title: Special Topics in Inorganic Chemistry

CHEM 721.description: Theory and application of classical and modern electrochemical techniques.
CHEM 721.subject: CHEM
CHEM 721.title: Electroanalytical Chemistry

CHEM 722.description: A comprehensive study of the theory, instrumentation, methodology, and analytical applications of modern atomic and quantitative molecular spectrometry.
CHEM 722.subject: CHEM
CHEM 722.title: Spectrochemical Methods of Analysis

CHEM 723.description: Theory and application of modern techniques for analytical separation and detection. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 723.subject: CHEM
CHEM 723.title: Separation and Detection Methods in Analytical Chemistry

CHEM 724.description: Survey of modern analytical chemistry with an emphasis on fundamental principles that govern sensitivity, selectivity, and speed of analysis. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 724.subject: CHEM
CHEM 724.title: Advanced Analytical Chemistry and Instrumentation

CHEM 729.description: May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 729.subject: CHEM
CHEM 729.title: Special Topics in Analytical Chemistry

CHEM 731.description: A study of the field of polymer chemistry including synthesis, characterization, and chemical and physical properties. Three lecture hours per week.
CHEM 731.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 334 or equivalent second semester organic chemistry.
CHEM 731.subject: CHEM
CHEM 731.title: Introduction to Polymer Chemistry

CHEM 732.description: This course covers important concepts for understanding the behavior and characterization of polymers.
CHEM 732.subject: CHEM
CHEM 732.title: Nanoscale Behavior and Characterization of Polymers

CHEM 733.description: This course covers important concepts for understanding the structures and physical properties of polymers.
CHEM 733.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in CHEM 731; C or better in CHEM 541.
CHEM 733.subject: CHEM
CHEM 733.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymers

CHEM 735.description: Basic concepts of structure, bonding, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms as applied to organic compounds and synthetic transformations.
CHEM 735.subject: CHEM
CHEM 735.title: Structural and Mechanistic Organic Chemistry

CHEM 736.description: A continuation of CHEM 735 with special emphasis on organic synthesis.
CHEM 736.subject: CHEM
CHEM 736.title: Mechanistic and Synthetic Organic Chemistry

CHEM 739.description: May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 739.subject: CHEM
CHEM 739.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry

CHEM 741.description: A development of classical thermodynamics and its application to chemical changes.
CHEM 741.subject: CHEM
CHEM 741.title: Chemical Thermodynamics

CHEM 742.description: The principles of surface processes – structure and electronic properties, adsorption and reactions, surface characterization using spectroscopy and microscopy.
CHEM 742.subject: CHEM
CHEM 742.title: Surface Science

CHEM 743.description: An introduction to the application of quantum mechanics to problems in chemistry.
CHEM 743.subject: CHEM
CHEM 743.title: Quantum Chemistry

CHEM 744.description: Calculations of the thermodynamic properties of chemical systems from molecular properties. Theory and applications.
CHEM 744.subject: CHEM
CHEM 744.title: Statistical Mechanics

CHEM 745.description: Point and space groups. Matrix representation and the derivation of the space groups. Significance of general and special positions. Powder and single crystal methods. Limitation imposed upon molecules by space group considerations. Introduction to structure analysis. Patterson and electron density functions. Refinement techniques.
CHEM 745.subject: CHEM
CHEM 745.title: Introductory Crystallography

CHEM 747.description: Study of the rotational, vibrational, and electronic spectra of polyatomic molecules for the elucidation of molecular structures.
CHEM 747.subject: CHEM
CHEM 747.title: Spectroscopy and Molecular Structure

CHEM 749.description: May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 749.subject: CHEM
CHEM 749.title: Special Topics in Physical Chemistry

CHEM 751.description: A detailed consideration of the enzymological basis for the synthesis of DNA, RNA, and protein including mechanisms for the regulation of these processes. Focus will be on eucaryotic mechanisms though procaryotic systems will be covered as necessary for background.
CHEM 751.subject: CHEM
CHEM 751.title: Biosynthesis of Macromolecules

CHEM 752.description: Biochemical organization of the cell. Regulation and integration of metabolism. Membrane structure and function. Energy transduction processes.
CHEM 752.subject: CHEM
CHEM 752.title: Regulation and Integration of Metabolism

CHEM 753.description: An analysis of the isolation, composition, structure, and function of enzymes emphasizing their kinetic, mechanistic, and regulatory features. Protein chemistry: amino acid and protein sequence analysis; chemical modification methodologies; analysis of higher order structures of proteins.
CHEM 753.subject: CHEM
CHEM 753.title: Enzymology and Protein Chemistry

CHEM 754.description: First of a two-semester sequence covering the major areas of biochemistry in a biomedical context. Chemistry of amino acids and proteins, enzymology, metabolism of carbohydrates and lipids. Emphasis is on biomedical research applications. Four lecture hours per week.
CHEM 754.subject: CHEM
CHEM 754.title: Biomedical Biochemistry I

CHEM 755.description: A continuation of CHEM 754 . Topics include nucleic acids and protein biosynthesis, blood chemistry, respiration, acid-base chemistry, metabolism, and nutrition. Four lecture hours per week.
CHEM 755.subject: CHEM
CHEM 755.title: Biomedical Biochemistry II

CHEM 759.description: May be repeated as content varies by title.
CHEM 759.subject: CHEM
CHEM 759.title: Special Topics in Molecular Biochemistry

CHEM 790.description: A laboratory and introduction to modern research techniques. Six hours of laboratory per week and individual consultation with instructor.
CHEM 790.subject: CHEM
CHEM 790.title: Introduction to Research

CHEM 791.description: A continuation of CHEM 790 . Six hours of laboratory per week and individual consultation with instructor.
CHEM 791.subject: CHEM
CHEM 791.title: Introduction to Research

CHEM 798.description: Directed laboratory research and readings in chemistry.
CHEM 798.subject: CHEM
CHEM 798.title: Research in Chemistry I

CHEM 898.description: A continuation of CHEM 798 for Ph.D. candidates.
CHEM 898.subject: CHEM
CHEM 898.title: Research in Chemistry II
